methodological_rigor.justification: The design is a secondary analysis of a Phase 2 TNT trial (n=37) with 5-fold cross-validation and a semi-supervised extension to n=118 using pseudo-labels. Strengths include a defined reference standard (radiologist-refined), inter-rater benchmarking with a fellow, pre-processing documented in Python/SimpleITK, bootstrap BCa 95% CIs with 10,000 resamples, and both parametric and non-parametric paired tests. Important limitations: no external/holdout test set (same n=37 evaluated across models), small sample size for radiomic clustering (416 features vs ~37 patients, highly susceptible to overfitting), no multiplicity correction across many pairwise DSC comparisons and 1317 radiomic features, no formal statistical test linking the unsupervised clusters to cCR status, no power calculation for the segmentation endpoint, and Model 3 post-treatment DSC (0.175) is notably poor. The acknowledgment that paired t-test vs Wilcoxon give discordant results (p=0.58 vs 0.008) is honest but highlights unaddressed distributional issues. Pseudo-label training risks circularity since Model 1 pseudo-labels propagated the radiologist's style, likely inflating Model 2's radiologist agreement.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: LoE 4 is appropriate: this is a small single-center retrospective secondary analysis of a Phase 2 trial cohort used for model development without external validation, functioning essentially as a case series for prediction-model development. Clinical topic (identifying cCR to support organ preservation in LARC) is highly important, and the use of patient-relevant outcome stratification (cCR vs non-cCR) is appropriate, but endpoints are limited to segmentation agreement and exploratory radiomic clustering rather than clinically validated prediction performance. The translational path is plausible but requires substantial validation; authors appropriately frame this as feasibility/proof-of-concept.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is most applicable as this is a prediction/segmentation model development study (REMARK/STROBE partially apply to the radiomic biomarker component). Key TRIPOD items addressed: participants/setting, predictors (imaging modalities), outcome definition (cCR), model development approach, and performance metrics with CIs. Gaps include no clear statement of handling missing data, no calibration or decision-curve analysis, no formal internal-validation versus apparent-performance distinction, no reporting of segmentation performance by cCR status, and no sample-size justification for model development. Code is reportedly on a public GitHub (redacted in blinded version) with versioned Python/PyTorch stack, but imaging data is not stated as publicly deposited; model weights are claimed public — reproducibility posture is reasonable but not exemplary.

novelty_literature.justification: Novelty is incremental: nnU-Net is an established framework; semi-supervised learning via pseudo-labeling is well-established in medical image segmentation; MRI-based radiomics in rectal cancer treatment-response prediction has been reported extensively in the literature. The specific combination (nnU-Net + pseudo-labels + ADC radiomics in a TNT trial cohort) is a reasonable extension, and the parallel documentation of post-treatment segmentation challenges in both humans and models is a useful empirical observation. The paper does not strongly position itself against the substantial existing literature on rectal MRI radiomics for TRG/cCR prediction, which limits the originality claim.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized, clearly written, and uses precise terminology with acronyms expanded on first use (TNT, cCR, DSC, LARC). The abstract is quantitatively grounded and faithful to the results. Figures and tables are described with informative captions that are largely self-contained, including numerical DSCs for representative cases. The discussion thoughtfully contextualizes limitations (post-treatment challenges, single center, segmentation/radiomic modality mismatch) and avoids over-claiming. Minor issues: Equations 1 and 2 are referenced in text but not reproduced; some paragraphs in the discussion are repetitive on the fibrosis/post-treatment theme.

key_strengths: Honest and thorough reporting of limitations including the discordant t-test vs Wilcoxon results and poor post-treatment DSC
Clear demonstration that semi-supervised learning with pseudo-labels improves pre-treatment segmentation to match inter-rater agreement (DSC 0.769 vs 0.748)
Reference standard established by radiologist refinement with independent fellow benchmark for inter-rater variability
Bootstrap BCa 95% CIs and dual parametric/non-parametric testing provide appropriate uncertainty quantification
Code and model weights reportedly available on public GitHub with versioned Python/PyTorch stack
key_concerns: Very small sample (n=37 reference cases, 9 cCR events) with no external validation limits generalizability
Radiomic clustering with 416 features in ~37 patients risks severe overfitting; no formal statistical test links clusters to cCR status
No multiplicity correction despite 1317 radiomic features and multiple pairwise segmentation comparisons
Post-treatment segmentation (Model 3, DSC 0.175) performs well below the already-poor inter-rater agreement (DSC 0.362), undermining the post-treatment radiomic pipeline
Semi-supervised improvement likely reflects circular reinforcement of the radiologist's style (97.3% of cases improved vs radiologist, only 59.5% vs fellow)
Novelty is incremental; the paper does not adequately position itself against the extensive existing rectal MRI radiomics literature
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically competent feasibility/proof-of-concept with transparent limitations, but small single-center sample, lack of external validation, concerning post-treatment performance, and incremental novelty place it at Tier 3 (specialty oncology/imaging journals). Minor revisions warranted to add formal cluster-cCR statistical testing, address multiplicity, and clarify the circularity in pseudo-label evaluation.
